title: chore: upgrade `unocss@66.4.2` and `@iconify/utils@3.0.1`
body:
## :bookmark_tabs: Summary

Brief description about the content of your PR.

Resolves #6791

## :straight_ruler: Design Decisions

Describe the way your implementation works or what design decisions you made if applicable.

`unocss@66.0.0` to `unocss@66.4.2` https://github.com/unocss/unocss/compare/v66.4.1...v66.4.2

I'm not entirely sure if this will break the program, but according to [antfu's previous article](https://antfu.me/posts/epoch-semver), this should be equivalent to the release rules for version 0.66.4-2, so it doesn't appear to break the program. But, it still needs to be evaluated by someone familiar with it.

- `@iconify/utils@2.1.0` to `@iconify/utils@2.3.0`  There seems to be no changes to the API we use.
- `@iconify/utils@2.3.0` to `@iconify/utils@3.0.1` https://github.com/iconify/iconify/pull/390

The focus is only on giving up cjs, which does not affect mermaid, because [Mermaid is ESM only!](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/releases/tag/v10.0.0)

Changesets that add features should be `minor` and those that fix bugs should be `patch`. Please prefix changeset messages with `feat:`, `fix:`, or `chore:`.

comments.body:
Any reason the `^` removed from the version, pinning it to `3.0.1`?
Same with unocss
comments.label_reasoning: The comment questions the intentional pinning of dependency versions (removing the `^` caret), which relates to dependency management and project configuration decisions rather than a defect or style issue.

comments.author: sidharthv96
comments.body: If we're moving `"@iconify/utils"` to v3, we need to check if we need to update `"@iconify/types"` as well.

comments.author: RSS1102
comments.body: The missing `^` was my mistake. `"@iconify/types"` does not need to be upgraded and cannot be upgraded. Its last version is [`2.0.0`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@iconify/types/v/2.0.0). It is the package that provides icon name types.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: The comment questions the removal of the `^` caret from the version specifier, implying that it should be restored to allow semver-compatible updates rather than pinning to an exact version.
